brief: US and European equities sold off Wednesday: SPX -75bps to 7706 (10 of 11 sectors lower), 2Y UST at 4.9%, highest in 2 years. Almost half of SPX constituents now carry a negative beta to the index, an all-time high; this raises momentum-unwind risk even as it adds index-level diversification. Equities historically react once the 10yr posts a 2-standard-deviation move, roughly 50bps over a month or 30bps over two weeks; the 10yr is up ~25bps in 2 weeks and 35bps in the past month, nearing that threshold. Flow: asset managers and hedge funds were each $1bn net sellers, managers selling macro, healthcare, tech and energy against consumer-discretionary demand, funds selling communication services and industrials against tech and healthcare demand. Stock calls: Haleon (Conviction Buy) forecasts +3.3% organic sales growth; ABI reframed its medium-term target to +5-9% organic EBIT growth from +4-8% EBITDA growth; PUIG (Conviction Buy) cites durables growth and a valuation discount to peers; H&M's 3Q EBIT beat consensus by 17% but was in line excluding a one-off SEK900m tariff refund, trading +1% versus a roughly +1.7% street view; Ceres Power (Conviction Buy) reiterated confidence in a new manufacturing licence deal and recognizing revenue in FY26.
